title: cb8b00171 1..8
one_sentence_summary: This study engineered pH-responsive M2pep analogues for acidic M2-macrophage targeting using amino acid substitution and solid-phase synthesis, titration, serum-stability testing, and flow-cytometric binding assays, finding that 3,5-diiodotyrosine and tetrafluorophenol substitutions enabled stronger low-pH-selective binding—with improved serum stability and reversible pH-dependent elution—although disubstituted analogues showed greater high-concentration toxicity.

experiments.title: 3,5-Diiodotyrosine-engineered M2pep pH-dependent binding
experiments.variables: Engineered M2pep binding to M2 macrophages at pH 6 versus pH 7.4
experiments.outcome: The engineered peptide showed greater selectivity for M2 macrophages under acidic conditions than at physiological pH.
experiments.evidence: Our engineered pH-responsive M2pep (Ac-Y-I-Î ) binds target M2 macrophages more selectively at pH 6 than̂ at pH 7.4.

experiments.title: Serum stability of 3,5-diiodotyrosine-substituted peptide
experiments.outcome: The substitutions improved peptide serum stability.
experiments.evidence: In addition, 3,5-diiodotyrosine substitutions also improve serum stability of the peptide.

experiments.title: Effect of histidine and 3,5-diiodotyrosine substitutions on M2pep pH-dependent binding
experiments.technique: Amino acid substitution of M2pep followed by pH-dependent binding assessment
experiments.variables: Histidine and 3,5-diiodotyrosine substitution variants and their pH-dependent binding activity
experiments.outcome: The study tested whether these substitutions confer pH-dependent binding; no result is reported on this page.
experiments.evidence: we investigate, in this study, the effect of histidine and 3,5-diiodotyrosine substitution(s) in an M2 macrophage-targeting peptide (M2pep) on pH-dependent binding activity.

experiments.title: pH-dependent binding of M2pepBiotin and AcM2pep(RY)Biotin to polarized macrophages
experiments.technique: Concentration-dependent peptide-binding assay on M1 and M2 macrophages
experiments.variables: M2pepBiotin versus AcM2pep(RY)Biotin; M1 control versus M2 macrophages; pH 6 versus pH 7.4; peptide concentration
experiments.outcome: Both peptides retained M2-over-M1 selectivity at both pH values; M2pepBiotin favored pH 7.4, whereas AcM2pep(RY)Biotin showed a weaker, concentration-dependent tendency toward greater binding at pH 6.
experiments.evidence: Both M2pepBiotin and AcM2pep(RY)Biotin bind to M2 macrophages with good selectivity over M1 macrophages at both pH 6 and 7.4, whereas M2pepBiotin binds to M2 macrophages with higher affinity at pH 7.4 than at pH 6; the effect of pH on binding activity of AcM2pep(RY)Biotin is less consistent and appears to be concentration-dependent, slightly favoring binding at pH 6 as the peptide concentration is increased (Figure 2).

experiments.title: Effect of the K9H substitution on M2pep pH-dependent binding
experiments.technique: Comparative peptide-binding assay on M2 macrophages
experiments.variables: M2pep(H9)Biotin versus original M2pepBiotin; pH 6 versus pH 7.4
experiments.outcome: K9H reversed the pH preference so that binding was stronger at pH 6, but the difference was marginal and overall affinity was reduced relative to the original peptide.
experiments.evidence: Indeed, a reverse trend in binding activity of M2pep(H9)Biotin on M2 macrophages was observed where the peptide binds more strongly at pH 6 than at 7.4 (Figure 3). Nonetheless, the difference in binding activities at these pH values is relatively marginal, and the overall binding affinity of the peptide is reduced compared to that of the original M2pepBiotin.

experiments.title: 3,5-Diiodotyrosine substitution engineering of low-pH-selective M2pep binding
experiments.technique: 3,5-Diiodotyrosine substitution by Fmoc/tBu solid-phase peptide synthesis followed by pH-dependent M2-macrophage binding assessment
experiments.variables: Tyrosine substitution position and pH-dependent binding to M2 macrophages
experiments.outcome: Appropriate tyrosine-to-3,5-diiodotyrosine substitutions produced engineered M2pep variants with low-pH-selective binding to M2 macrophages.
experiments.evidence: Specific to M2pep, we found that appropriate substitutions of tyrosine with 3,5-diiodotyrosine resulted in desirable low pH-selective binding activity of the engineered M2pep to target M2 macrophages.

experiments.title: pH-dependent binding of disubstituted M2pep(R9) analogues
experiments.variables: Dual 3,5-diiodotyrosine substitutions at positions 1 and 12 or positions 10 and 12; pH 6 versus pH 7.4; disubstituted versus monosubstituted analogues
experiments.outcome: Both disubstituted analogues further increased binding while retaining low-pH selectivity.
experiments.evidence: Botĥ disubstituted analogues show further enhancement in binding activity over the monosubstituted ones while also retaining good low-pH selectivity (Figure 4B).

experiments.title: High-concentration toxicity assessment of substituted M2pep(R9) analogues
experiments.technique: Toxicity observation during peptide binding-curve measurements
experiments.variables: Peptide concentration; monosubstituted versus disubstituted analogues
experiments.outcome: Toxicity at higher concentrations prevented accurate binding-curve and pH-selectivity determination, and disubstituted analogues were more toxic.
experiments.evidence: Toxicity of these peptides was observed at higher concentrations, preventing us from accurately constructing the binding curves to determine KD,7.4/ KD,6 for quantitative comparison of pH selectivity of each analogue (data not shown).

experiments.title: Effect of N-terminal acetylation on macrophage binding and M2-to-M1 selectivity
experiments.technique: Peptide-binding assay with M1 and M2 macrophages
experiments.variables: Free versus acetylated N-terminus; M1 versus M2 macrophages; pH 6 versus pH 7.4
experiments.outcome: Acetylation did not noticeably alter binding; low pH increased M1 binding, but binding remained substantially lower than on M2 macrophages.
experiments.evidence: For both peptides, an increase in binding activity on M1 macrophages is observed at pH 6, but the extent of binding remains substantially lower compared to that on M2 macrophages.

experiments.title: Synthesis of a tetrafluorophenol-substituted M2pep analogue
experiments.variables: Replacement of the terminal tyrosine with the tetrafluorophenol-functionalized residue
experiments.outcome: A tetrafluorophenol-bearing analogue was synthesized to test an alternative physiologically ionizable tyrosine mimic.
experiments.evidence: we synthesized Ac-Y-Y-- , where the last tyrosine residue was replaced with 2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-4-hydroxybenzoic acid-functionalized 2,3-diaminopropionic acid (- ) (Figure 6A).

experiments.title: Acid titration of the tetrafluorophenol-substituted analogue
experiments.variables: Tetrafluorophenol group in Ac-Y-Y-- versus 3,5-diiodotyrosine in Ac-Y-I-I
experiments.outcome: The tetrafluorophenol group had an estimated pKa comparable to the 3,5-diiodotyrosine group, approximately 7.5–8.
experiments.evidence: A pKa value of - on Ac-Y-Y-- was estimated from an experimental acid titration curve and was found to be comparable to I ̂ on Ac-Y-I -Î ̂ (7.5−8) (Figure S1).

experiments.title: pH-dependent binding of the tetrafluorophenol-substituted analogue
experiments.variables: Ac-Y-Y-- versus AcM2pep(RY)Biotin; pH 6 versus pH 7.4
experiments.outcome: The tetrafluorophenol analogue bound M2 macrophages more strongly at pH 6 and showed enhanced affinity relative to AcM2pep(RY)Biotin.
experiments.evidence: Ac-Y-Y-̂ - binds to M2 macrophages more strongly at pH 6 compared to its binding activity at pH 7.4 (Figure 6B).

experiments.title: Reversible pH-dependent elution of bound Ac-Y-I-Î
experiments.technique: Postbinding peptide-elution assay on M2 macrophages with median fluorescence intensity readout
experiments.variables: Initial binding in PBSA at pH 6 followed by post-treatment incubation at pH 6, 7.4, or 8.5
experiments.outcome: Median fluorescence intensity decreased as post-treatment pH increased, indicating pH-dependent elution of bound peptide.
experiments.evidence: Indeed, we observed a reduction in median fluorescence intensity read-out as a function of increasing pH, which indicates the pH-dependent elution of the bound peptides off the target (Figure 7B).

experiments.title: Synthesis and molecular-weight confirmation of peptide analogues
experiments.technique: Fmoc/tBu solid-phase peptide synthesis, HPLC purification, and MALDI-ToF mass spectrometry
experiments.variables: Peptide sequence and chemical modification, including 3,5-diiodotyrosine-containing and acetylated analogues
experiments.outcome: The synthesized peptides were purified and their molecular weights were confirmed.
experiments.evidence: Molecular weights of the synthesized peptides were confirmed by MALDI-ToF MS.

experiments.title: Peptide binding to polarized primary macrophages at pH 6 and 7.4
experiments.variables: M1 versus M2 macrophage polarization; binding and wash-buffer pH 6 versus 7.4; peptide treatment
experiments.outcome: Peptide binding was measured by flow cytometry after incubating polarized macrophages under the investigated pH conditions.
experiments.evidence: All washing steps and incubations were performed in buffers at the desired pH under investigation (pH 6 or 7.4).

experiments.title: Cell-viability control during flow-cytometric binding studies
experiments.outcome: Cell viability was assessed before flow-cytometric analysis of every sample.
experiments.evidence: Propidium iodide was added prior to running of each sample to assess for cell viability.

experiments.title: Peptide serum-stability time course
experiments.technique: Incubation in normal mouse serum followed by peptide extraction and MALDI-ToF mass spectrometry
experiments.variables: Incubation time in normal mouse serum
experiments.outcome: Peptide degradation patterns were analyzed at multiple time points.
experiments.evidence: At different time points, an aliquot (40 μL) was drawn, mixed with an equal volume of ACN to precipitate serum proteins, and centrifuged at 10,000 rpm for 5 min.

experiments.title: Supplementary titration curves of Ac-Y-Y-- and Ac-Y-I-Î
experiments.outcome: Titration curves for both peptide analogues were provided in the Supporting Information.
experiments.evidence: Titration curves of Ac-Y-Y-- and Ac-Y-I -Î ̂

experiments.title: Supplementary competition binding of M2pep-displayed M13 phages
experiments.variables: M2pep analogues used in competition with M2pep-displayed M13 phages
experiments.outcome: Competition binding between M2pep-displayed phages and M2pep analogues was evaluated in the Supporting Information.
